source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Boot into UEFI shell.
2. Command: SMBIOSVIEW > File.log

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Check there is no Wistron string in the log.

original_test_intent: Verify from a complete pre-OS SMBIOS dump that prohibited Wistron identity strings are absent and the owner-intended Cisco replacements are present in the correct structures/fields.
original_method: An operator runs a compatible SMBIOSVIEW in UEFI Shell and preserves complete File.log; afterward the artifact is scanned under an owner mapping/encoding policy with every match keyed to SMBIOS context.
manual_activity: Generating and attesting the complete pre-OS UEFI dump is manual; the agent can scan and compare the supplied artifact but cannot perform the source execution.
required_inputs: Wistron prohibited variants and Cisco expected replacements by field
Complete unfiltered log and console evidence
safety_requirements: Run SMBIOSVIEW read-only; do not mutate SMBIOS or flash firmware.
Preserve the full unfiltered log before any search and record its hash/size.
Do not infer positive Cisco replacement from absence of one Wistron spelling.
Stop on truncated output, encoding ambiguity or wrong tool/platform; no automatic rerun.
agent_execution_scope: Hash and scan the supplied full log under exact/case/encoding policies, report every prohibited match with structure context and compare expected Cisco mappings.
Collect supporting OS/BMC identity/health without claiming UEFI execution or verdict.
engineer_actions: Run SMBIOSVIEW in UEFI Shell and preserve complete console/log evidence.
Approve mapping/exceptions and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It correctly states that OS SSH cannot perform the source UEFI action; no substitute command is appropriate.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved UEFI tool manually and automate only read-only scanning of the complete returned artifact.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact SMBIOSVIEW redirection and 5/5-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Preserve a complete hashed UEFI dump and validate prohibited/expected strings by SMBIOS structure/field, not by one global literal absence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BIOS/SMBIOS build and branding policy.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, SMBIOS and SMBIOSVIEW versions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds positive replacement checks, encoding policy and context.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects missing Cisco replacements, case/encoding variants and inappropriate strings in OEM/non-product fields.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A text dump may render binary/OEM data imperfectly; ambiguous occurrences require raw context or RD review.

project_override_considerations: Projects may define permissible third-party strings and exact Cisco values, but must disclose exceptions and cannot claim full replacement from only a negative grep.
expected_evidence: Platform/tool identity and approved mapping policy
All Wistron matches and expected Cisco field comparisons
Encoding/OEM exception decisions and health logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title's positive replacement claim is broader than the negative criterion, but expected Cisco mapping can be supplied as a readiness input without changing the procedure.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The pre-OS workflow is clear; manual source execution makes it MANUAL ONLY rather than blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps the manual UEFI boundary and strengthens semantic evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains complete-log and positive/negative mapping safeguards.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates automated artifact analysis from manual execution and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a false success when Wistron disappears but the intended Cisco identity is missing, misplaced or encoded differently.
independent_technical_reasoning: Brand replacement is a field-level transformation, not merely a global negative string property; complete UEFI evidence plus an explicit source-to-target mapping is required.
